\begin{paperabstract}
We characterize the search space of keyboard layouts (30! $\approx$ 2.65 $\times$ 10³²
placements) with a random-walk correlation analysis, a local-optima
network sampled by breakout local search, and a MAP-Elites map over
ergonomic behaviours. {[}TODO: fitness-distance correlation value;
number of funnels; fraction of local optima within 1 \% of best; Pareto
front shape.{]} Popular community layouts {[}TODO: lie on / behind{]}
the front. We release the atlases and a viewer.

\end{paperabstract}
\begin{paperbody}
\section{Research questions}

RQ1 Big-valley or multi-funnel? (FDC, funnel decomposition.) RQ2 How
many distinct near-optimal layouts exist and how different are they
(Hamming, finger distance, swap distance)? RQ3 What do you pay to get
more rolls or less index load (QD, Pareto)? RQ4 Where do the
\textasciitilde4,100 community layouts sit on the map?

\section{Hypotheses}

H1 positive FDC (big valley). H2 a few funnels differing in vowel
placement. H3 the number of near-optimal optima $\gg$ the number of used
reference layouts. H4 the roll/SFB front is short and convex.

\section{Method}

\texttt{gecko\ landscape} (random distribution, correlation length),
\texttt{gecko\ explore} (10 min $\times$ 10 seeds per setting),
\texttt{gecko\ atlas} (families, consensus, funnels),
\texttt{gecko\ qd\ -\/-axes\ roll\_ratio,index\_load\ -\/-bins\ 16},
\texttt{gecko\ optimize\ -\/-algo\ nsga2}. Canonicalize under left/right
mirroring only when provably symmetric. Community layouts from
\texttt{data/community/cmini.json}, scored on the same tables.

\section{Existing evidence}

Space statistics and distance definitions
(\texttt{research/studies/search-space-visualization.md}); exploration
and QD specs (\texttt{context/algorithms/explore.md},
\texttt{map-elites.md}).

\section{Figures}

F1 local-optima network · F2 FDC · F3 score density vs optima · F4
autocorrelation · F5 consensus keyboard and contested slots · F6
MAP-Elites heatmap with references and community density · F7 Pareto
fronts.

\section{Threats}

Sampling bias of BLS (kicks define the network edges); results are for
one profile (see paper 2); the descriptor choice shapes the QD map.

\end{paperbody}
